signals.title: FIRST 60 KAWASAKI KLE500 CUSTOMERS TO RECEIVE EXCLUSIVE MEGATRAIL ADVENTURE PA...
signals.summary: New middleweight adventure motorcycle priced at RM32,900, with a 150km off-road ownership experience in Gerik, Perak The KLE500 is available in a Metallic Carbon Gray, Ebony and Frame Flat Black colour scheme. Shah Alam, Malaysia , 4 August 2026 – Motosikal dan Enjin Nasional Sdn. Bhd. (“MODENAS”), a member of the DRB-HICOM Group, has announced an exclusive Kawasaki KLE500 Megatrail promotion for the first 60 customers in Malaysia, following the commencement of its digital launch campaign on 3 August 2026. Priced at a recommended retail price of RM32,900 , excluding insurance and road tax, the KLE500 is Kawasaki’s latest offering in Malaysia’s growing middleweight adventure segment. The promotion is available from 3 to 31 August 2026 at authorised Kawasaki dealerships nationwide. Designed for daily commuting, long-distance touring and off-road exploration, the KLE500 combines a 451cc parallel-twin engine with long-travel suspension, 21-inch front and 17-inch rear spoke wheels, selectable ABS and rally-inspired styling. Its upright ergonomics, three-position adjustable windshield and 16-litre fuel tank provide a balanced combination of comfort, control and versatility across varying road and terrain conditions. Roslan Roskan, Chief Executive Officer of MODENAS, said the KLE500 reflects Kawasaki’s commitment to delivering product enjoyment throughout the ownership journey. “The KLE500 gives riders a versatile and capable platform to explore beyond their everyday routes. signals.title: Before manufacturers discovered influencers, Triumph made this viral masterpiece
signals.summary: Motorcycle marketing has changed beyond recognition, but this classic Triumph Rocket III video remains as absolute comedy gold. Before social media algorithms, before influencers, before every bike launch needed a cinematic drone shot and someone dramatically staring into the middle distance, Triumph quietly released what might still be the funniest motorcycle video ever made. You may also like to read our Triumph Rocket 3 review . Originally uploaded back in 2007 to promote the then-new Rocket III Classic, the spoof factory documentary has somehow aged better than plenty of modern motorcycle marketing campaigns. Presented as a serious behind-the-scenes look inside Triumph's production line, the video quickly descends into the kind of glorious nonsense that has us waiting for Basil Fawlty to appear. Engines are tested to the sound of banjo music "for safety purposes", workers carefully harvest chrome from fields, and the bike's legendary handling is apparently thanks to "argument juice" extracted from the female brain. And as for the 2,300cc engine which is apparently “grown from embryo engines, germinated in a nutrient-rich sludge medium” and then left in a cupboard by the photocopiers. It's exactly the sort of deadpan British humour that made me fall in love with British comedy back in the 80s and 90s. From The Fast Show to Vic and Bob’s Big Night Out, this piece of comedic artwork was a perfect snapshot of where UK comedy was at the time. We first shared the clip on Visord

signals.title: Kawasaki Z500 / Z500 SE: fresh colours for my 2027
signals.summary: The technicians from Akashi have updated the Z500 and Z500 SE for 2027. While keeping its fierce Sugomi styling and sharp technical DNA untouched, the big update brings a fresh wave of striking new graphics and colour combinations. The standard Z500 for 2027 is proposed in Ebony / Metallic Carbon Gray, whereas the Z500 SE is available in Candy Persimmon Red / Metallic Carbon Gray or Pearl Blizzard White / Candy Lime Green Type 3 / Ebony. Underneath the tank beats the 451cc twin-cylinder engine pushing out 45 hp, designed specifically for A2 license riders. Its trellis frame champions agility and mass centralization, while the low 785 mm seat height, active riding position, and wide handlebars guarantee both comfort and total control. An Assist & Slipper clutch keeps lever action light while preventing rear-wheel hop and lock-ups during rapid downshifting. On the technology front, the Z500 relies on clean LCD instrumentation, while the SE raises the bar with a vibrant TFT display featuring a digital speedometer and tachometer, gear position indicator with shift lamp, dual trip meters, and instant or average fuel economy readouts.
